Seattle, Again

memories below

Gray Matters

The trip began in an airport parking garage, where the sun was setting behind the Front Range in streaks of orange and slate. That same night I was back at Pike Place Market, watching the red PUBLIC MARKET neon glow above Elliott Bay, with strings of white bulbs running along the awning beside it. A STREET CLOSED sign hung on the lamp post out front. The neon, at least, was open for business!

Saturday began at first light on a working pier. Across the bay, the arches of Lumen Field and the port's red cranes sat under a long, dark bank of cloud, with a sliver of moon still up. Turn toward downtown and the picture changed: fog had swallowed the towers from the top down, and the teal building stamped with a giant white 66 was the only splash of color. Down the waterfront, the Seattle Aquarium's Ocean Pavilion, which opened in 2024, hangs a tropical reef over its entrance. An oval window in the underside lets anyone walking by stand beneath it and look up into the water, no ticket needed, so that is what I did, head tipped back. Coral crowds the rim, fish cross the rippling blue, and the whole thing glows like a skylight into a warmer ocean.

Sunday settled into steel gray and stayed there. A ferry crossed the bay in front of the container cranes while gulls worked the air above it, and the Great Wheel stood against the clouds with a red crane showing through its spokes. The water looked far too calm to have a past, but during the last ice age this whole bay lay under roughly half a mile of glacier. Everything I could see, the ferry, the cranes, even the Wheel, is a very recent arrival on the scale of that story.
